agentControl.description: Lets this device start and stop external agent processes on this desktop. The spawn policy still limits which programs may run, from which folder, and with which environment — but within those limits the device chooses. Remote control is a separate, lesser grant.
agentControl.reason: Confirm letting {label} run agents on this desktop
agentControl.title: Allow running agents

browserAccess.title: Browser access
browserAccess.description: A browser can't verify this computer's self-signed certificate, so the usual HTTPS port is unreachable from a tab. This opens a plain http://127.0.0.1 listener — the one address a browser trusts without a certificate. It stays on this machine and never leaves it.
browserAccess.restartRequired: Restart the Companion server to apply.
browserAccess.loadFailed: Browser access settings could not be read.

origins.title: Allowed browser origins
origins.description: Only these exact origins may reach this computer. Anything else is refused — including the same address on a different port.
origins.empty: No origin is allowed yet, so browser access does nothing until you add one.

blocked.loopbackOnly: Bound to this machine only — switch the server to LAN.
blocked.serverStopped: The companion server is not running.

channels.description: Every route a paired device can use to reach this desktop, and whether it currently works.
channels.desktopOnly: Reachability can only be tested from the desktop app.
channels.title: Channels

lockedComputerUse.description: Grants this device Locked Use — a short, task-bound unlock lease. Not active yet: the macOS Locked Use system component is not part of this build, so this switch grants nothing until it ships.
lockedComputerUse.title: Allow Locked Use

logto.awaitingCode: A browser window opened. After you authorize, paste the full redirect URL (or just the code) below.
logto.description: Sign in to your Logto tenant so this desktop can act as an authenticated client of the cloud / headless companion gateway.

errors.codeMalformed: Could not read a code from that input. Paste the full redirect URL or the code value.
errors.missingFields: Issuer, client ID, API resource and redirect URI are all required.
errors.profileBoundToAnother: This local profile is already signed in as {name}. Sign out of this profile before signing in as someone else.
errors.stateMismatch: The pasted callback does not match this sign-in attempt. Start again.

field.personNone: Not linked to a Cognia account yet

logto.storageFallback: Signed-in tokens are stored in an encrypted vault in this browser or app rather than the operating system keyring.
logto.title: Logto cloud sign-in

toast.hostMirrorFailed: Signed in, but this desktop could not record who you are. Pairing keeps working; try again once the companion service is running.

mdns.description: Broadcast _cognia._tcp on the LAN so phones find this desktop without QR scan.
mdns.title: LAN auto-discovery (mDNS)

pair.accountLocked: Unlock a local account before pairing a device.
pair.codeHint: Type this on the phone when scanning the QR isn't practical (e.g. Android emulator without camera passthrough).
pair.description: Generate a QR code, scan it with the cognia mobile app, and the phone exchanges the one-shot token for a long-lived device JWT.
pair.expired: Token expired — refresh to issue a new one.
pair.title: Pair a new device

paired.description: Pause temporarily blocks a device; revoke is permanent and biometric-gated. Both deny-list the JWT immediately.
paired.empty: No devices paired yet — generate a QR to add one.
paired.title: Paired devices
paired.toastPaused: {label} paused. Its JWT is rejected until resumed.

pause.description: The device's JWT is added to the deny-list until you resume it.
pause.title: Pause device

push.apnsKeyPlaceholder:
-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
...contents of the .p8 file...
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----
push.description: Paste FCM (Android) and APNs (iOS) credentials to enable push delivery for paired phones while their WebSocket is disconnected. Secrets are stored in the OS keyring on desktop; headless deployments use a JSON file under the data directory.
push.desktopOnly: Only available in the Tauri desktop build.
push.fcmPlaceholder: Paste the '{"type":"service_account",...}' JSON downloaded from Google Cloud Console.
push.fcmRequired: Paste the FCM service-account JSON first.
push.title: Push notifications

pushTokenFailed: Couldn't tell the desktop about this phone's push token ({reason}).

remoteBrowser.description: Run an isolated Chromium session on the paired workspace runtime and stream it to Cognia.

domains.description: Only explicitly granted domains may be opened by this workspace.
domains.title: Allowed domains

remoteBrowser.gateHint: Both this setting and the server rollout gate must be enabled.
remoteBrowser.operationFailed: The remote browser setting could not be saved.

profiles.description: Persistent profiles retain browser state inside the selected workspace.
profiles.name: Profile name
profiles.title: Browser profiles

remoteBrowser.title: Remote browser
remoteBrowser.unreachableHint: No Cognia server is connected, so these profiles and domains have nothing to run in yet.
remoteBrowser.workspaceHint: Select a workspace before managing profiles or domains.

remoteControl.description: Lets this device drive and steer live agent sessions on this desktop, and approve computer-use prompts. Read-only sync stays available either way.
remoteControl.title: Allow remote control

remoteTerminal.description: Lets this device view, resume, and control host-owned terminal sessions. This permission is independent from remote control and agent control.
remoteTerminal.operationFailed: The terminal permission could not be saved.
remoteTerminal.title: Allow terminal access

resume.description: The device's JWT is removed from the deny-list and regains access.
resume.title: Resume device

server.desktopOnly: Companion server runs in the desktop process — switch to the Tauri build to manage it.
server.httpsWarning: Self-signed HTTPS is active. The mobile client pins the cert fingerprint encoded in the QR; a server cert rotation requires re-pairing.
server.lanDesc: Required to actually pair a phone. Reachable on every interface on the local network.
server.loopbackDesc: Safest. The companion API is only reachable from the desktop itself — useful for testing the QR flow.
server.serverOff: Server is off. Phones cannot reach this device.
server.title: Mobile companion server

syncStatus.description: Per-table sync state. The orchestrator pulls deltas sequentially; use Sync now to force a single table.
syncStatus.title: Sync status

tunnel.description: Reach this desktop from anywhere. Requires the cloudflared CLI to be installed.
tunnel.namedConfigured: Named tunnel configured. Toggle to start cloudflared.
tunnel.notInstalled: cloudflared not found — install via brew/winget/apt first.
tunnel.off: Off. Turning the switch on launches cloudflared as a subprocess.
tunnel.title: Cloudflared tunnel

webrtc.description: Third transport tier (ADR-0021). Uses role-authenticated signaling and end-to-end encrypted envelopes, so the rendezvous cannot read SDP or ICE.

descriptions.awaiting: Subscribed to the rendezvous, waiting for the mobile peer to join.
descriptions.connected: DataChannel is open. The phone reaches the desktop directly.
descriptions.failed: Last session ended in error. The client task is backing off before its next attempt.
descriptions.negotiating: Mobile peer joined; exchanging SDP and ICE candidates.
descriptions.offline: Signaling client is idle — usually between reconnect attempts.

webrtc.enableHelp: When on, the mobile app reaches this desktop directly via WebRTC after pairing — falling back to LAN or the cloudflared tunnel only when WebRTC can't open.
webrtc.iceServersHelp: One stun: URL per line. Public STUN is enough for most home networks; add more if NAT traversal stalls.
webrtc.invalidUrl: Signaling URL must start with ws:// or wss://
webrtc.noDevices: No paired devices with WebRTC enabled yet. Pair a phone running the latest mobile build to populate this list.
webrtc.pollFailed: Couldn't read the signaling hub status ({reason}). The device list below may be stale.
webrtc.reconnectThrottled: Slow down — wait a few seconds between reconnects.
webrtc.signalingUrlHelp: WebSocket endpoint for the public rendezvous. Self-hosted deployments swap this for their own URL.
webrtc.title: WebRTC remote access
webrtc.turnProviderHelp: Optional. Auto-mints short-lived TURN credentials and rotates them before expiry, instead of pasting static ones above. The API secret is stored in the OS keyring, never in plaintext.
webrtc.turnProviderTokenStored: Token stored — enter a new one to replace
webrtc.turnServersHelp: Required only for symmetric NAT. Format: one `turn:host:port|username|credential` per line. Credentials are stored in the OS keyring — bring your own (Twilio, Cloudflare, coturn), or use the automatic provider below.
webrtc.turnTestSuccess: TURN provider OK — {count} ICE servers, valid until {expiresAt}.

collaboration.title: Collaboration server
collaboration.help: Where this profile's shared issues, workspaces and membership come from. Sign in above first — the server identifies you by that session, and the organisation comes from it too.

skipped.not-configured: No collaboration server is set for this profile.
skipped.not-signed-in: Sign in above before refreshing — the server identifies you by that session.
skipped.no-org: You are signed in, but this account belongs to no organisation, so there is nothing shared to pull.

browserCompanion.title: Browser Companion
browserCompanion.description: Pair the Cognia browser extension with this computer. Once paired, a page you capture in your browser starts a new task here — nothing is read until you capture it.
browserCompanion.requiresListener: Browser access is off, so a pairing code would have nothing to connect to. Turn it on above and restart the Companion server first.
browserCompanion.generateFailed: The pairing code could not be created.
browserCompanion.codeLabel: Paste this into the extension's side panel
browserCompanion.copyFailed: The code could not be copied. Select it and copy it by hand.
browserCompanion.expired: This code has expired. Generate a new one.
browserCompanion.singleUse: One use only. It is spent the moment an extension redeems it, and it carries no credential on its own.
browserCompanion.originHint: After installing the extension, add its chrome-extension:// origin to the list above. The extension shows it on its connection screen.
browserCompanion.pairedHint: Paired browsers appear in the device console, where you can revoke one.
